mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand in the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased construction activity and related sectors.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2% in a single month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate increased consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate potential monetary tightening and reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a single month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both real GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) show a simultaneous increase over a 3-month period, it signals a robust expansion in economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased economic activity and related sectors.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both increase > 1% over 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between GDPC1, HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
